title: Threshold sensitization quiet window causing hidden capacity gaps
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: During a multi-region weekend surge (2025-01-18 -> 2025-01-19) several small-to-medium tenants experienced silent throughput degradation on Dedicated reserved pools. Requests were accepted but saw elevated queuing and token-level throttles without clear pool depletion alerts. Customers reported elevated latency and 429s on short chat bursts.

What happened: The autoscaler includes a 'quiet_window' heuristic that suppresses noisy short-lived scale signals while the system is stabilizing. A recent change to the spike-detection smoothing (alpha parameter went from 0.25 -> 0.05) meant short but sustained microbursts were smoothed out and not surfaced as scale events. At the same time the admission controller's burst-bridge logic constrained temporary headroom because a new admission gating change prioritized fairness for high-cardinality tenants. The combination produced a hidden capacity gap: the system thought pools had headroom when, for the affected tenants, effective enqueue latency had already breached burst SLAs.

Impact: Multiple customers on Dedicated (not on Hosted) experienced degraded tail latency and transient 429s for burst patterns with high token-per-request cost. Several escalations to Support/Success during the weekend; two customers opened urgent tickets and requested credits. No data exfiltration or security exposure.

Root cause (investigation summary):
- Regression introduced by smoothing parameter change in spike detector (commit: github.com/redwood/realtime/commit/fe3a1d2).
- Quiet_window gating logic was too coarse-grained; it used a single-timescale EWMA across tenants instead of a per-tenant quantile estimator.
- Admission controller change (fairness gating) reduced temporary burst headroom for medium tenants during AZ-level pressure.
- Telemetry blindspot: enqueue-latency histogram was not aggregated at tenant granularity for the affected metric, so alarms did not fire.

Immediate mitigations (hotfixes shipped):
- Reverted smoothing alpha to 0.25 for spike-detector (hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood/realtime/pull/1893) — rolled out to prod AZs within 90 minutes of detection.
- Emergency feature flag to bypass quiet_window for tenants flagged as "urgent-warmup" (control plane flagging; roll forward enablement PR: https://github.com/redwood/controlplane/pull/1125).
- Short-term admission controller tweak: temporary relax fairness gating thresholds for dedicated pools until we're confident estimator changes are stable.

Planned permanent fixes and follow-ups:
- Replace EWMA per-tenant smoothing with a lightweight quantile sketch (P98/P95) for spike detection to avoid over-smoothing microbursts. (ENG task scheduled, estimate 8).
- Enhance enqueue-latency histograms to be tenant-scoped and add alerting rules for tail-latency anomalies. (observability epic).
- Rework admission controller's burst-bridge logic to allow controlled ephemeral headroom increases for warmup bursts while preserving multi-tenant fairness.
- Add an automated canary that runs synthetic microburst traffic against Dedicated pools during deploy windows to detect quiet_window regressions.
- Runbook updates: expand Dedicated capacity troubleshooting doc with a 'hidden-gap' section and playbook steps for emergency bypass flags. (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Dedicated+Autoscale+Runbook)

2025-01-19: 09:40 UTC - Hotfix PR created and validated in staging: https://github.com/redwood/realtime/pull/1893
2025-01-19: 10:15 UTC - Hotfix rolled to prod (canary AZ) and then rollout to all Dedicated regions. Observed drop in tenant enqueue latency and 429s within ~20 minutes post-rollout.
